summary:
Parallax is a web observatory we built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps challenge “Planet X and SPHEREx.” It lets anyone search for a sky position, open real infrared observations from NASA’s SPHEREx mission, and compare images of the same field over time. Users can play exposures in date order, compare observations at similar wavelengths, and inspect the original FITS files and observation metadata.
Satellite View helps users choose where to look, while 3D Context places selected objects in their astronomical surroundings using catalog positions and distances. Together, these tools make it easier to explore the sky and investigate possible motion or brightness changes using the underlying observations.
details:
Explore the infrared sky with Parallax, our project for the 2026 NASA Space Apps challenge “Planet X and SPHEREx.” Search a sky position, play real SPHEREx observations in date order, and compare exposures to see what changed. Inspect a frame’s wavelength and quality information, or switch from Satellite View to 3D Context to see where a target sits among nearby stars.

SPHEREx observations are provided through Caltech/IPAC’s NASA Infrared Science Archive. The Satellite View sky backdrop uses NASA Goddard’s Deep Star Maps.
